results.title: Is Dr. the same as Doctor? Or how to distinguish these two?
results.content: # [Is Dr. the same as Doctor? My co-worker argued that Dr. means Doctor (as a job), while I translate it to Dr (as a title, like Master, bachelor, doctor). I think Dr is, of course, short for Doctor, which can be both a title or a job. P/S: Also, does `Dr.` as a title has anything relate to those in `{Master, Doctor, Bachelor}`? 'Dr.' is simply an abbreviation for the title 'Doctor'. Dr. should not be used to abbreviate the word 'doctor' when it is not a title, though you might find it used like that in older writings. Doctor and Dr. would be more of what you would've been thinking is Title, or Name. The example I gave for the nurse extends to other disciplines; I know people with doctorates in bioengineering and physical therapy who use the title: "Mr." It seems that it's mostly the academics that like to retain the "Dr." title.
